title: Problem 1.1 (Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov)
statement_text: Show that for any $q \geq 2$, there exists $c_q$ such that $r_3(H; q) \leq 2^{2^{c_q\sqrt{m}}}$ for any 3-uniform hypergraph $H$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices.
context_text: Conlon, Fox and Sudakov proved that any $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with $m$ edges satisfies $r_k(H; q) \leq \mathrm{tw}_k(c\sqrt{m\log m})$ for $k=3$, and asked whether the logarithmic factor could be removed. This problem was posed in their survey on graph Ramsey theory.
paper_contribution: Resolves Problem 1.1 in full: Theorem 1.2 proves $r_k(H; q) \leq \mathrm{tw}_k(C_{k,q}\sqrt{m})$ for all $k \geq 3$ and any fixed number of colors $q$, with a unified proof covering all uniformities.
paper_title: Ramsey numbers of hypergraphs of a given size

title: Informal Problem: extending the $\sqrt{m}$ Ramsey bound to more than two colors for graphs
statement_text: It would be interesting to extend the result $r_2(G; 2) \leq 2^{c\sqrt{m}}$ (for any graph $G$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices) to more than two colors.
context_text: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ and an integer $q$, $r_k(H;q)$ is the $q$-color Ramsey number: the minimum $N$ such that every $q$-coloring of the edges of the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph $K_N^{(k)}$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$; so $r_2(G;q)$ is the usual $q$-color Ramsey number of a graph $G$. Erdős and Graham conjectured that among graphs with $m=\binom n2$ edges the clique $K_n$ has the largest Ramsey number; Erdős made the weaker conjecture that $r_2(G;2)\le 2^{c\sqrt m}$ for every graph $G$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, which is sharp by the lower bound $r_2(n;2)>\sqrt2^{\,n}$ for cliques. Sudakov proved this conjecture, but his argument only works for two colors. The present paper proves the hypergraph analogue for every fixed number of colors: for $k\ge 3$ and fixed $q$, every $k$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices has $r_k(H;q)\le\mathrm{tw}_k(C_{k,q}\sqrt m)$, where $\mathrm{tw}_1(x)=x$ and $\mathrm{tw}_k(x)=2^{\mathrm{tw}_{k-1}(x)}$, tight for $q\ge4$ (resolving a problem of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov); the graph case $k=2$ with $q\ge3$ colors is what the remark leaves open, the natural target being $r_2(G;q)\le 2^{c_q\sqrt m}$ for every graph $G$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices.
notes: Stated as a brief remark in the introduction without a labelled environment.
paper_title: Ramsey numbers of hypergraphs of a given size
